note: init_log_file: 'if !enabled { return None }' inside prepare_path skips creating the log file/dir entirely when logging is disabled - a real early-out, not just a data store.
visit_arrow: 'if is_describe { (None, None) } else { parse_test_context_param(...) }' decides whether to parse a Deno.test step-context param, since describe blocks don't take one.

denormalize_inner: alias_node_modules genuinely gates 'if alias_node_modules && !specifier.contains(...)' - a real branch - but this is the *already-refactored* shape the rule recommends: two public wrappers (denormalize, denormalize_with_node_modules_alias) hide the flag from every caller, and only this private shared-impl helper takes it directly. Flagging the private helper undercounts how well this call site actually follows the guidance.
resolve_compile_executable_output_path: 'if is_desktop' (further down, deciding output-path defaults/extension) selects desktop-app vs regular-binary output naming conventions.
confirm_package_trust: 'if yes { return Ok(None) }' skips the interactive trust prompt when --yes was passed - the doc comment names the flag's exact purpose.
setup_config_dir: 'if force { ... }' (comment: 'When --force is specified, the user is explicitly asking for a fresh ...') overwrites existing config rather than reusing it.
serve_http: 'if wait_for_connection' (deep in the spawned task) decides whether the connection-serving future is awaited synchronously or just spawned and returned immediately.
write_: fromEnd is branched on three times (a ternary and two 'if' guards) distinguishing writes from OutgoingMessage.end() vs a regular .write() call - Node's http_outgoing.js internal shape.

setBroadcast: 'arg ? 1 : 0' serializes the bool into the native SO_BROADCAST socket-option int - same data-serialization shape as tcp.rs's apply_keepalive_socket; also a Node.js dgram API-compat method, so the exact signature (setBroadcast(arg: boolean)) is fixed by Node's own API, not renameable.
unwrapErr: 'if (!ok) throw new ERR_CRYPTO_HASH_FINALIZED()' - ok is a result/error-signal flag whose falsy value throws; a small helper wrapping a native call's boolean success return.
parseKeyType: 'if (typeStr === undefined && !required) { return undefined }' short-circuits validation when the type is optional - Node.js crypto key-parsing polyfill.

getKeyTypes: 'else if (!allowKeyObject) { return ArrayPrototypeSlice(types, 0, 5) }' - allowKeyObject (alongside the earlier bufferOnly check) selects which prefix of the accepted-key-types list is returned for an error message.

indexOfBuffer: forwardDirection is branched on repeatedly ('if (!forwardDirection && offset >= searchEnd)', 'else if (forwardDirection && ...)', an OR operand deciding search-window bounds) - real forward-vs-backward Buffer.indexOf/lastIndexOf search direction logic (mirrors node_buffer.cc).

apply_keepalive_socket: 'let on: c_int = if enable {1} else {0}' serializes the bool into the C setsockopt on/off int - same data-serialization shape as the k8s addBool/deno-elsewhere cases, not a caller-facing behavior-mode choice.

write_response_head_inner: chunked (after being narrowed by HTTP version) gates 'if chunked && body_allowed { write transfer-encoding: chunked header }' and an earlier content-length-vs-chunked exclusivity check.
begin_object_key: implements serde_json's Formatter trait (fixed external signature, first: bool is not renameable here) - 'if first {"\n"} else {",\n"}' picks the separator before a JSON key.

append_bat_arg: quote is mutated and rebranched multiple times ('if quote { quote = true }' escalation logic based on content, then 'if quote' twice to actually emit quote chars) - genuine multi-step decision logic, not a simple setter.

mockConsole's Console printer callback: same 'printsNewLine ? "\n" : ""' ternary as the other console_test.ts instance - both are legitimate uses of Deno's real Console printer-callback boolean parameter.

consoleGroupForwardsLabelToWrappedLog's mock printer lambda: 'out.add(x + (printsNewLine ? "\n" : ""))' - a real Console-callback-signature bool parameter (matches Deno's actual Console printer callback shape), directly ternary'd.

writeHttp2Data: 'endStream ? 0x01 : 0' directly encodes the HTTP/2 END_STREAM wire-protocol flag bit - same data-serialization shape as the addBool/tcp.rs cases (the bool literally *is* the wire flag, not a caller-facing mode choice).
helloWorldStream: 'if (close == true) { controller.close() }' - optional close?: boolean param gates whether the test stream auto-closes after its first chunk.
emptyStream: onPull picks whether the test stream closes immediately in start() (!onPull) or on the first pull() (onPull) - doc comment: 'closes either immediately or on a call to pull'.

tlsWithTcpFailureTestImpl: 'reverse ? {tlsConn1: tlsClientConn, ...} : {tlsConn1: tlsServerConn, ...}' - a destructured ternary swapping which side plays client vs server for the test, confirming ternary conditions (not just if-statements) are correctly caught.

testRespondWithCancellation: ownsFd is branched 3 times ('ownsFd ? undefined : fs.openSync(...)', 'if (ownsFd)', 'closeCalls, ownsFd ? 1 : 0') to test both respondWithFd-owns-the-fd and caller-owns-the-fd code paths.

set_buffer: 'if enabled { Some(Vec::new()) } else { None }' is a simple on/off state-toggle setter (test-capture buffer), same idiomatic-setter shape as the already-marked ripgrep skip_stdout/crlf cases.
